en.sup: Supplied in English. The Greek has no verb in this clause.

01.r: Sets the time when the giving applies.
01.n: In the KJV, ASV and YLT this verse opens with 'but by (an) equality', words that our text, as this brief gives it, places at the end of the verse before; the Geneva's verse begins later still, at 'That also their aboundance'. This is a difference of verse division.

02.r: The article that makes 'now' into 'the present'.

03.r: The time Paul is writing in.
03.n: Abbott-Smith: 'now, i.e. at the present time'; with the article and a noun, 'the present'.

04.r: The present season, as against a later one when the roles may change.
04.n: Abbott-Smith gives first 'due measure, fitness, proportion', then, of time, 'a fixed and definite period, time, season'.

06.r: The Corinthians, to whom Paul writes.

07.r: What the Corinthians have beyond their own needs.
07.n: Abbott-Smith derives it from περισσεύω and gives 'that which is over and above, superfluity, abundance', and he sets it as the opposite of ὑστέρημα, the 'lack' later in this verse; he cites this verse and the one before.

08.r: The abundance goes toward filling the others' lack.
08.n: With no verb in the clause, this 'for' carries the sense of direction and purpose; the translations supply 'may be a supply for', 'will meet' and similar.

10.r: The believers in need, elsewhere than Corinth.
10.n: Literally 'of those', a pronoun that points to people at a distance, as opposed to 'you'. Who they are is not named in this verse.

11.r: What the others are short of.
11.n: Abbott-Smith derives it from ὑστερέω and gives 'that which is lacking, deficiency, shortcoming'.

12.r: Gives the purpose of the present giving.
12.n: Abbott-Smith: its proper use is final, 'denoting purpose or end, that, in order that'.

13.r: The giving may one day run the other way.

15.r: The same distant believers, now pictured as the ones with more.

16.r: What the others may one day have to spare.

17.r: Looks to a future turn of events, not a certainty.
17.n: A subjunctive of the verb Abbott-Smith gives as 'to come into being, be born, arise'; the ASV's 'may become' keeps that sense.

18.r: Their abundance would then go toward the Corinthians' lack.

21.r: What the Corinthians may one day be short of.

22.r: States the final aim of the exchange.
22.n: A second word of purpose; Abbott-Smith gives 'in order that, to the end that, that'. Our English uses 'that' here and 'so that' above to keep the two words apart.

23.r: Equality is the outcome Paul aims at.

24.r: Neither side having too much while the other has too little.
24.n: Abbott-Smith derives it from ἴσος, equal, and lists this verse under 'equality'; his second sense, 'equity, fairness', he gives for another passage.
